Explain the example for turn on foreign-key checks

blocks.text: A foreign key links a child record to a parent id. SQLite needs foreign-key checking enabled for a connection to enforce the link.
Use the SQL Run button for examples marked runnable. They use this site's in-browser SQLite database and sample-only table names. A Python example needs Python on your own computer instead.

blocks.title: Turn on foreign-key checks

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A primary key identifies a row and prevents duplicate key values. Related records can refer to that key.
`PRAGMA` is SQLite's command family for connection settings or inspection. Check the specific pragma's effect.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The valid child row refers to reader 1. A row referring to a missing parent would be rejected with checks enabled.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Set the pragma before starting a transaction. Confirm the setting for each new connection.
